meta.title: A Real-Time Framework for Prompt Injection Attacks Detection on Cloud-Hosted Large Language Models

problem.v: Detect and block prompt injection at gateway of cloud-hosted LLMs in real time

main_idea.v: Fine-tuned DistilBERT classifier served on AWS SageMaker; blocks malicious prompts at gateway above 0.85 confidence; telemetry to CloudWatch

threat_model.v: Malicious input prompts (information leakage, privilege escalation, output manipulation, jailbreak)

datasets_benchmarks.name: Annotated prompts, 2500 benign + 2500 malicious, augmented with security terms

results.claim: Per attack type F1: leakage 0.95, privilege escalation 0.92, output manipulation 0.93, jailbreak 0.89

results.number: ~220 ms inference; ~60% cost reduction (text claim, no table)

limitations_inferred: [INFERENCE] Reports precision/recall only, no FPR/AUC at low-FPR operating points (contrast P03)
[INFERENCE] Possible train/test leakage: data was augmented before splitting (p3 'After augmentation, the data was split')
[INFERENCE] DistilBERT F1 0.92 does not match P=0.96,R=0.92 (harmonic mean ~0.94)
[INFERENCE] Latency/cost claims lack supporting table; no end-to-end attack-success evaluation

reusable_for_our_project.v: Reference AWS architecture (S3 model artifact, SageMaker endpoint via boto3, gateway blocking, CloudWatch telemetry, threshold 0.85) for our deployment stage; code repo to adapt

flags: F1 arithmetic mismatch for DistilBERT row
Abstract claims precision superiority only; DeBERTa-v3 has higher recall and F1
